name: beyond_load_schema
description: Load all entity and processor schemas for the current Platform project. Use once at session start and again before coding from confirmed design so the AI can cache the current schema for auto-completion and code generation. Keep this schema, including each processor's transformations, in the AI's temporary or working context while coding. Returns schema without lineage details; each returned processor also includes its transformations. Compact mode still includes stable ids such as entity_id, processor_id, and attribute_id in their natural enclosing objects.

include_relationships.description: Include FK relationships for JOIN suggestions

names_and_data_types_only.description: When true, return a compact schema for entity and processor attributes including attribute_id plus core fields such as names and data types, while parent entity_id or processor_id remains on the enclosing object.

canvas_ids.description: Limit to specific canvases. Empty = all accessible

response_format.description: auto returns inline when small and switches to paged delivery when the response exceeds max_inline_bytes. full disables automatic paging. paged forces paged delivery.

max_inline_bytes.description: Maximum serialized structuredContent size to return inline when response_format is auto.

page_size_bytes.description: Maximum JSON text fragment size per page when paged delivery is used.

include_json_content.description: When false, omit duplicated JSON from text content and rely on structuredContent.

assignment_item.description: Value assignment for INSERT/UPDATE. Creates WRITE lineage.

source_attributes.description: If value comes from another attribute

constraint.description: Constraint definition. Used for create/update payloads and for persisted constraint records.

constraint_type.description: Constraint type. For pgvector vector similarity indexes, use 'cosine', 'l2', or 'inner_product' instead of generic 'Index'. These map to pgvector cosine, L2, and inner-product operator classes.

columns.description: Column names involved in the constraint

check_expression.description: For CHECK constraints only. Do not use this for Unique constraints or partial unique indexes.

constraint_value.description: For Default or Check constraints, the stored value or condition

constraint_order.description: Attribute order within the constraint for persisted records

index_type.description: For generic INDEX constraints. For pgvector vector similarity indexes, prefer constraint_type 'cosine', 'l2', or 'inner_product' instead of encoding the vector index as a generic Index.

other_info.description: Preserved relationship metadata. on_delete/on_update are reference annotations, not supported BE behaviors.

relationship_description.description: Stored relationship description, separate from referential-action metadata.

metadata_guide.description: Present when on_delete or on_update metadata exists; explains that BE does not support or apply these behavior settings.

attribute_name.description: Logical attribute name. Use a human-friendly business/property name in the user's language, not a physical identifier.

domain_id.description: Optional domain ID applied to this attribute

data_length.description: Physical length/size for the data type. For vector-like types this is the embedding dimension; for bit and bit varying this is the bit length.

decimal_points.description: Scale / decimal precision for numeric data types. Do not use this for vector, bit, or bit varying.

data_type.description: Physical data type exposed as data_type

nested_data_type.description: Logical nested element type for complex attributes

nested_physical_data_type.description: Stored physical data type for nested values

encryption_level.description: Integer levelNumber: 0=NONE (None), 1=MASKED (Masked), 2=ENCRYPTED (Encrypted), 3=HASHED (Hashed; one-way hash), 4=KEYSERVER (Key Server; encryption key managed by a key server). Writes do not accept null; omission preserves the value on modification.

sensitivity_level.description: Custom sensitivity level defined by the organization. 0 = not specified, 1 = public, 2 = internal, 3 = confidential, 4 = restricted

confidentiality.description: TARA confidentiality classification. L = Low, M = Medium, H = High, S = Safety Critical.

integrity.description: TARA integrity classification. L = Low, M = Medium, H = High, S = Safety Critical.

availability.description: TARA availability classification. L = Low, M = Medium, H = High, S = Safety Critical.

other_info.description: Additional JSON metadata for the attribute

upper_attribute_id.description: Parent attribute ID for nested structures. Null for root-level attributes.

pii_data_type.description: PII_DATA_TYPE enum name stored verbatim, e.g. DRIVER_LICENSE. Null clears the classification; this is independent of pii_level.

encryption_level_desc.description: Human-readable encryption_level: None, Masked, Encrypted, Hashed, Key Server; null for an undeclared value.

auto_created_constraints.description: Constraints automatically created while creating this entity, such as PrimaryKey from is_primary_key or Default from default_value. Do not create these constraints again.

anyOf.description: Logical lineage graph page with coverage and continuation.

lineage_status.description: Lineage coverage only (separate from inventory/search pagination). complete means this single response includes the whole selected traversal; traversal_complete means traversal finished across all graph pages. focused is policy-limited. Follow continuation.tool/cursor until exhausted; combine all prior pages. A depth/path/state limit requires a narrower or deeper new query.

auto_created_attributes.description: Attributes automatically added from storage-type default_fields; also included in attributes. Do not create them again.

entity_info.description: Entity metadata returned by MCP read tools.

entity_name.description: Logical entity name. Use a human-friendly business name in the user's language. Do not default this to a physical identifier.

other_info.description: Additional JSON metadata for the entity

endpoints.description: Verified inbound HTTP routes for a Controller class or API Server boundary. One Controller processor can contain multiple path/method/handler combinations. Omit unknown fields; never assume GET or derive routes from class names. On update omission preserves, an array replaces, [] empties, null clears. Do not use for Filter/Interceptor matching or Advice scope. Stored only in other_info.endpoints; the top-level response is a projection, not a separate stored value. API Server represents one Swagger/OpenAPI operation: endpoints is an array with at most one method/path pair. Different methods or paths require separate processors. Spring Controller classes may have multiple endpoints. Endpoint cardinality follows the storage catalog: is_module=true permits multiple endpoints; false, null or omitted permits at most one. Clients cannot override this flag. This applies to all processor types and both endpoints and other_info.endpoints. Check acceptable_processors or processor_storage_types before writing. Legacy JSON strings encoding an array or null are also accepted, decoded and validated; new writes store arrays or null and top-level endpoints read projections use arrays or null. Existing raw other_info may retain legacy strings until updated. New clients must send arrays. Invalid strings are rejected without clearing metadata.

path.description: Verified request mapping path; resolve class and handler mappings only from evidence.

method.description: Verified HTTP method; omit if unspecified or unknown. Never default to GET.

handler.description: Actual source handler method name without class/package prefix; omit if unknown.

endpoint_id.description: Server-assigned stable Controller endpoint ID. Preserve on edits to retain the contract association.

input_attribute_id.description: Server-managed Controller INPUT Object ID. Preserve on edits; do not invent. Same-handler routes share this ID.

output_attribute_id.description: Server-managed Controller OUTPUT Object ID. Preserve on edits; do not invent. Add verified child fields under this Object.

Use 'pgvector' for dedicated pgvector tables, and use 'postgresql' or 'supabase' when vector or bit columns belong to those runtime models. For vector and bit attributes, data_length represents dimensions or bit length, and decimal_points should not be used. For InfluxDB entities, entity_name should describe the business meaning of the series and table_name should store the physical series signature based on tag-key combinations. Save sample tag/field text in other_info.

model.description: Top-level design container for a system boundary in Beyond Entity. A model can represent a database/warehouse schema, a browser or app UI/task design surface, or a general system boundary for APIs, processor groups, files, caches, applications, or mixed components.

model_storage_type.description: Storage/system type for the model. Use database values such as 'postgresql', 'pgvector', or 'bigquery' only for real persisted data platforms. Use 'pgvector' for dedicated PostgreSQL pgvector vector databases and embedding stores; PostgreSQL and Supabase models can also contain vector or bit columns when those data types are present in the entity schema. Use 'webapp' for browser-based user workflows and screens such as signup, login, search forms, and modal/page interactions. Use 'app' for application UI workflows and screens such as product lists, detail pages, dashboards, and mobile app navigation. Use 'rabbitmq' or 'kafka' for messaging-system boundaries. Use 'influxdb' for InfluxDB time-series models, where database_name represents Bucket and schema_name represents Measurement. Use 'general_system' for backend, API, file, cache, integration, or processor-centric system groupings; use entity_storage_type='general_file' inside general_system for unstructured or mixed file resources. Store exchange/topic/binding/partitioning or other platform-specific settings in other_info when needed. Use model_storage_type='spring_boot_application' for legacy Spring Boot, Spring AI, and Spring MVC (including non-Boot MVC). When extracting architecture from code, use the actual class name as processor physical name/module_name; exclude its package and record verified package_name, qualified_class_name and source_file in other_info for class tracing. Choose the closest matching allowed spring_boot_* processor type, such as spring_boot_controller or spring_boot_service; use module_general for an unmatched class/module or processor_general for an individual operation. Use model_storage_type='google_workspace' for Google Workspace resources and automation. Query beyond_get_definitions(definition_names=["model_selection_guide"]) for the full rules and examples.

database_name.description: Physical database/schema/container name when the model represents a database-like platform. Optional. If omitted, defaults to model_name.

system_name.description: Logical system name exposed for non-database models such as 'general_system', 'webapp', 'app', 'rabbitmq', and 'kafka'. This must be a readable business-facing name such as 'Virtual Office API' or 'Virtual Office App', not a physical identifier like 'virtual_office_api'. In persistence this is backed by database_name; there is no separate system_name field in storage. Use the user's language for logical names: Korean for Korean users, Japanese for Japanese users, otherwise English.

storage_name.description: Optional storage container/group name used by modify/get flows.

partition_name.description: Optional partition name used by modify/get flows.

processor_name.description: Logical/business processor name. For api_server processors, use the user-facing API name; do not use HTTP method/path or code identifiers.

module_name.description: Physical/code identifier. projection_item.description: SELECT column mapping. Defines how a source attribute becomes a target attribute. This is the primary source of READ and TRANSFORM lineages. Wildcards such as '*' or 'alias.*' are authoring shorthand only and must not be sent as a single projection item. Use explicit SQL select items with beyond_add_transformation_by_sql so lineage can be created per column. Within one SELECT transformation, each projected source column must map to its own distinct target attribute unless you are using explicitly modeled nested child attributes.

projection_type.description: DIRECT=simple copy, FUNCTION=date/string func, VECTOR_DISTANCE=vector similarity/distance expression such as embedding <-> :query_embedding or COSINE_DISTANCE(embedding, :query_embedding), VECTOR_COMPARISON=boolean vector threshold expression such as embedding <-> :query_embedding < 0.8, AGGREGATE=SUM/COUNT in SELECT, COALESCE=null handling

source_attributes.description: Source attributes. Empty for COUNT(*) or literals. Do not use a single representative source attribute for '*' or 'alias.*'; wildcard projections must be expanded into the full relevant attribute list.

examples._description: Vector distance projection from pgvector/PostgreSQL/Supabase SQL

relationship_type.description: Required. Cardinality alone cannot determine optionality or identifying semantics. Choose one of the listed values explicitly.

from_entity_id.description: Child/referencing entity ID. Use this instead of from_table_name when you already have the entity ID.

to_entity_id.description: Parent/referenced entity ID. Use this instead of to_table_name when you already have the entity ID.

to_column_name.description: (Optional) Existing child table column name(s) to reuse for FK mapping. If omitted, new child FK columns are created based on the parent PK.

to_attribute_ids.description: Legacy form (no from_attribute_ids): CHILD FK IDs, despite the to_ prefix. Paired form with from_attribute_ids: PARENT PK IDs. Prefer explicit parent_attribute_ids/child_attribute_ids.

parent_entity_id.description: Explicit parent entity ID. Parent owns the PK; child owns the FK.

parent_attribute_ids.description: Existing parent attribute IDs, in matching pair order. Parent must supply the complete PK.

child_entity_id.description: Explicit child entity ID. Parent owns the PK; child owns the FK.

child_attribute_ids.description: Existing child attribute IDs, in matching pair order. Parent must supply the complete PK.

from_attribute_ids.description: Paired from/to form: CHILD FK IDs; to_attribute_ids then denotes PARENT PK IDs. Without this field, legacy to_attribute_ids denotes CHILD FK IDs.

on_delete.description: on_delete/on_update are NOT supported BE relationship behavior settings. Inputs are preserved only as reference metadata in relationship other_info. Creation and FK/relationship reads return other_info and metadata_guide when these keys are present. They may inform source SQL analysis or code/DDL authoring; BE does not apply or guarantee these rules. relationship_description remains the separate supported relationship description.

on_update.description: on_delete/on_update are NOT supported BE relationship behavior settings. Inputs are preserved only as reference metadata in relationship other_info. Creation and FK/relationship reads return other_info and metadata_guide when these keys are present. They may inform source SQL analysis or code/DDL authoring; BE does not apply or guarantee these rules. relationship_description remains the separate supported relationship description.

relationship.description: Create FK relationships. Prefer explicit child_entity_id/child_attribute_ids and parent_entity_id/parent_attribute_ids, plus required relationship_type. Parent IDs must cover the complete PK; child IDs are reused, not duplicated. Legacy from_entity_id=child, to_entity_id=parent; legacy to_attribute_ids (without from_attribute_ids) unusually denotes CHILD FK IDs. Paired from_attribute_ids/to_attribute_ids instead belongs to each matching entity. cardinality alone is insufficient; choose optional/mandatory/identifying explicitly. The tool creates the FK constraint and RELATION references; do not duplicate them with beyond_add_constraints. Each relationship is atomic; inspect created_relationships and failed, retry only failed items.

raw_expression.description: Original ORDER BY expression, including vector distance expressions such as d.embedding <-> :query_embedding.

source_attribute.description: A universal attribute reference. source_entity_id can point to a Table, File, Redis Key, Processor, or any other entity.

source_alias.description: Optional alias used in SQL (e.g., 'o', 'c', 'p'). If omitted, the server fills it from the source entity table/module name when possible.

source_model_id.description: Beyond Entity model ID. Optional if source_attribute_id or source_entity_id is provided; the server will resolve it when possible.

target_attribute.description: Reference to a target entity/processor attribute. target_alias and target_model_id may be omitted; the server will resolve them from the target entity/attribute when possible. For transformation projections or aggregations targeting the current processor, if target_attribute_id is omitted but target_entity_id and target_column_name are provided, the server may reuse an existing LOOKUP/OUTPUT attribute by column name or create a new LOOKUP attribute and populate target_attribute_id.

target_alias.description: Optional alias for the target entity or processor scope. If omitted, the server fills it from the target entity table/module name when possible.

target_column_name.description: Target column or attribute name. Required when target_attribute_id is omitted. For projections/aggregations into the current processor, this name is also used to resolve or auto-create a LOOKUP attribute.

target_attribute_id.description: Target attribute ID. Optional when target_entity_id and target_column_name are provided and the server can resolve or auto-create the target attribute.

target_model_id.description: Beyond Entity model ID. Optional if target_attribute_id or target_entity_id is provided; the server will resolve it when possible.

transformation.description: The logic engine of Beyond Entity. Maps data flow between Entities (Tables, Files, Caches) and Processors. Every transformation item automatically generates a Lineage record.

transformation_name.description: Human-readable name, e.g., '[T1] Fetch active orders'

semantic_level.description: (Optional) Semantic level of the transformation, which can guide how lineages are generated and visualized. RELATIONAL is traditional table-based operations. DOCUMENT is for document stores like MongoDB. KEY_VALUE is for key-value stores like Redis. GRAPH is for graph databases like Neo4j. VECTOR is for vector search or vector-distance operations such as pgvector similarity queries.

referring_raw_code.description: (Optional) Original SQL or code. Kept for reference and debugging.

other_info.description: (Optional) Additional information related to the transformation. json object where you can put any properties relevant to this transformation, such as database connection info, API endpoint info, code generation hints, etc.

sources.description: Source entities used in this transformation (FROM clause)

projections.description: SELECT mappings (for SELECT) or value expressions (for INSERT SELECT)

examples.referring_raw_code: SELECT o.order_id, o.total FROM orders o WHERE o.status = 'ACTIVE' AND o.created_at >= :startDate
INSERT INTO coupon_issue (coupon_id, customer_id, status, issued_at) VALUES (:coupon_id, :customer_id, 'ISSUED', CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)

examples._description: SELECT login candidate with one projection target per selected column
examples.referring_raw_code: SELECT id, username, password_hash, role FROM admin_users au WHERE au.email = :email AND au.is_active = TRUE

examples._description: SELECT with JOIN, aggregation, and grouping
examples.referring_raw_code: SELECT DATE_TRUNC(:groupBy, o.created_at) AS period, COUNT(*) AS order_count, SUM(o.amount) AS total_amount FROM orders o WHERE o.created_at >= :startDate GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC(:groupBy, o.created_at)

value_info.description: Value specification for filters and assignments

value_type.description: LITERAL=fixed value, PARAMETER=processor INPUT/LOOKUP, ATTRIBUTE=another entity column, EXPRESSION=complex SQL

value.description: For LITERAL: the value. For PARAMETER: :param_name format

value_entity_id.description: For PARAMETER: processor_id. For ATTRIBUTE: entity_id

comparison_operator.description: Optional comparison operator for compound expressions such as vector distance threshold filters. Example: lt for '<'.

comparison_right_operand.description: Optional right operand for compound expressions such as vector distance threshold filters. Example: 0.8 in 'embedding <-> :query_embedding < 0.8'.
